name: Liang Xiaolin
current_role: Shareholder of Dashenlin Pharmaceutical Group (SSE: 603233); wife of chairman Ke Yunfeng
profile: Liang Xiaolin is the wife of Ke Yunfeng, founder-chairman of Guangzhou-based Dashenlin (大参林), one of China's largest drugstore chains; Hurun lists the couple jointly. She holds about 9.8m Dashenlin shares directly; the family's wealth comes from the Ke brothers' controlling stake. No public executive role found for her.
interesting_fact: Dashenlin differentiates on ginseng and tonic herbal medicines ('参茸滋补') and runs 38 warehouses with an order-fill rate of 99% and error rate under 0.008%, per its 2024 annual report summary.
notes: Annual report confirms '梁小玲为柯云峰之妻'. Very low public profile; outreach should go through Dashenlin's board secretary/IR office (tel 020-81176091 published in same report).

name: Robert Hagedorn
current_role: General partner, Hagedorn Partnership L.P. (10%+ owner of The Scotts Miracle-Gro Co.)
profile: Son of Miracle-Gro founder Horace Hagedorn and brother of Scotts Miracle-Gro chairman/CEO Jim Hagedorn. His wealth stems from the family's stake in Scotts Miracle-Gro, created when Miracle-Gro merged with Scotts in 1995; he is one of the general partners of the Hagedorn Partnership, which holds roughly a fifth of SMG.
interesting_fact: His father Horace co-founded Miracle-Gro in 1951 with horticulturist Otto Stern and built it through direct-response ads; the 1995 merger with Scotts made the Hagedorns the largest shareholders of America's biggest lawn-and-garden company.
notes: Private, non-executive family shareholder; listed as a Hagedorn Partnership GP in 2025-26 Form 4s (with Chris Hagedorn, Katherine Littlefield, Nathan Baxter, Hope Reeves). 2005 obituary placed him in the Seattle area (Pacific Northwest). Best route is Scotts Miracle-Gro corporate communications/IR (investor.scotts.com).

name: Ding Lieming
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Betta Pharmaceuticals (SZSE: 300558), Hangzhou
profile: Medical researcher who spent about a decade studying and working in the US before returning to China in 2002 and founding Hangzhou-based Betta Pharmaceuticals, an oncology-drug maker. Betta's icotinib (Conmana), approved in 2011, was China's first home-grown small-molecule targeted cancer drug; he still leads the company as chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: The Lancet Oncology said icotinib 'has created the new era of China's R&D of anticancer drugs'; Ding priced it at roughly 60-70% of comparable imported drugs so more lung-cancer patients could afford it.
deep_cut_fact: He said he left the US because there he 'could not fulfill my dream to innovate and start my own business'; Betta started with only about 200,000 yuan of seed funding, and he set up a program giving free pills to patients still responding after six months on Conmana.
notes: Hurun lists him jointly with Ding Shizhe. Company contact email is general corporate (Tel +86-571-86130357 on same page). Founding year given as 2002 or 2003 depending on source.

name: Longling

name: Wang Yuedan
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Ningbo Fujia Industrial Co. (Furja, SSE: 603219), Yuyao, Zhejiang
profile: Wang Yuedan is chairman and actual controller (about 70% directly and via Fujia Holdings) of Ningbo Fujia Industrial, founded in 2002 in Yuyao, Zhejiang. Furja is an ODM maker of vacuum cleaners, cordless/wet-dry floor cleaners, robot vacuums and brushless motors, listed in Shanghai in 2021 and now expanding into Vietnam.
interesting_fact: Furja has made vacuums for Shark since 2004 and became JS Global/SharkNinja's largest supplier in 2018; that customer has long accounted for over 80% of its revenue.
notes: Low personal media profile. Company email is the listed corporate address (board office tel 0574-62838000). Interesting angle: Chinese ODM behind a major US appliance brand; its business scope now includes energy storage, PV and EV battery-swap equipment.

name: G Mason Morfit
current_role: Co-CEO and Chief Investment Officer, ValueAct Capital; director of Salesforce (since March 2023)
profile: Mason Morfit joined San Francisco activist fund ValueAct Capital at its 2000-01 inception, became CEO in 2020 (co-CEO with Rob Hale since 2024) and is known for 'quiet', board-level activism. He has sat on the boards of Microsoft, Valeant, C.R. Bard and others, and joined Salesforce's board in 2023 under a cooperation agreement.
interesting_fact: Morfit joined Microsoft's board in March 2014, shortly after Satya Nadella became CEO, as ValueAct's representative, and served there through Microsoft's early cloud pivot (left the board in 2017).
deep_cut_fact: Before ValueAct he was an equity-research analyst in Credit Suisse First Boston's health-care group covering managed care; today he also sits on the board of Tipping Point Community, the Bay Area anti-poverty nonprofit, and on Princeton SPIA's advisory council.
notes: ValueAct media line 415-362-3700 (Oct 2025 release). His Salesforce net-worth figure reflects ValueAct's holdings reported on insider filings. Feb 2026: ValueAct took a stake in BlackRock, framing it as a software (Aladdin) story - relevant to a data/AI-infrastructure podcast.

name: Yan Ming
current_role: Non-executive director and controlling shareholder (~23.7%), JF SmartInvest Holdings (HKEX: 9636), Shanghai
profile: Yan Ming co-founded Shanghai-based Yintech Investment Holdings (Nasdaq-listed 2016) with Chen Wenbin and Chen Ningfeng, and the trio are controlling shareholders of JF SmartInvest (九方智投), an online investment-research/education and stock-advisory platform that listed in Hong Kong in 2023. He has been a non-executive director there since August 2021.
interesting_fact: In 2025 JF SmartInvest moved into licensed brokerage by acquiring Yintech Financial, owner of Hong Kong's Forthright Securities and Forthright Capital - effectively reuniting the founders' earlier Yintech business with the listed company.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech, Yan spent 2003-2013 as general manager of Beijing Jinghua Times International Culture & Entertainment, and since 2018 he has chaired the Hong Kong Federation of Jiangxi Associations.
notes: Non-executive, low-profile. Holdings: Chen Wenbin 36.14%, Yan Ming 23.72%, Chen Ningfeng 21.10% (May 2025 HKEX circular). Deep-cut source is an aggregator (MarketScreener); verify before use. Education per company site: finance BA (Shanxi Univ. of Finance & Economics), EMBA (CKGSB).

name: Su Jianguo
current_role: Founder and actual controller, Jiangsu Leili Motor Co. (SZSE: 300660), Changzhou; son Su Da is general manager and legal representative
profile: Su Jianguo (b. c.1955) founded Changzhou-based Leili in 1993, when China's micro-motor industry was in its infancy, and built it into a major maker of motors for air conditioners and appliances (listed in Shenzhen 2017). Now run day-to-day by his son Su Da, Leili has diversified into EV motors, medical micro-motors (Dingzhi Technology) and robot components such as hollow-cup motors and dexterous hands.
interesting_fact: Before its 2017 IPO nearly 90% of Leili's revenue came from home-appliance motors; it has since opened a Vietnam plant (2019) and started mass-producing hollow-cup motors for robots in 2024, with a subsidiary (Zhongke Lingxi) building dexterous robot hands.
deep_cut_fact: Leili's first product was an air-conditioner motor, developed by an early technical team drawn largely from an established state-owned enterprise in Changzhou.
notes: Hurun pairs him with son Su Da, who now fronts the company and gives interviews (e.g. The Paper, July 2026) - Su Da is the better outreach target. A team-profile page (pitchhub.36kr.com) says Su started in 1979 as a salesman at Wujin No.3 Electronic Components Factory; verify against prospectus.

name: Chen Xiaohong
current_role: Early/founding-era individual shareholder of Glodon Co. (SZSE: 002410), holding ~79.2m shares (~4.8%) as of Q1 2026
profile: Chen Xiaohong is one of the original individual shareholders of Beijing-based Glodon, China's leading construction-cost and BIM software company (founded 1998 by Diao Zhizhong, listed 2010). She held about 10.6% at the time of the 2014 annual report and still holds roughly 4.8%; no current executive role was found.
interesting_fact: Glodon began by making cost-estimating software for construction quantity surveyors and has grown into China's main construction-digitalisation/BIM platform, now pitching 'industry AI' for engineering.
notes: Unlike co-founder Tu Jianhua, she has barely sold down (79.37m shares in 2014 vs 79.17m in Q1 2026). No public bio, interviews or role found; very private. Name is common (also a Hunan academician 陈晓红) - do not confuse. Route via Glodon board-secretary office.
